runs.text: China earns enough income to purchase large quantities of natural resources from developing countries.
Which statement explains this situation?

cells.text: China does not experience the economic problem of scarcity.
Supplies of natural resources in China are limited relative to demand.
There are unlimited supplies of natural resources in developing countries.
There is an excess stock of land in China.

runs.text: To help reduce the price of oil, new supplies are needed. However, in 2013, objectors opposed attempts to explore new sites because of the environmental damage the exploration might cause.
How does this illustrate the basic economic problem?

cells.text: Oil is a limited resource.
Oil is expensive.
The exploration involves demand and supply.
There are external costs involved in production.

runs.text: What is the basic economic problem?

cells.text: finite resources and limited wants
finite resources and unlimited wants
infinite resources and limited wants
infinite resources and unlimited wants

runs.text: Water is a scarce resource in Singapore because the island’s small geographical area means there is little land on which to collect water for its 4.8 million people.
Which method would be least successful in tackling its water scarcity?

cells.text: exempting large families from paying water taxes
importing water from neighbouring countries
introducing a water tax that rises as consumption rises
redirecting funds from education to schemes to purify rainwater

runs.text: Why is choice an important part of the basic economic problem?

cells.text: Choice is necessary to achieve an equilibrium price.
Limited resources have many uses.
Manufacturers produce a large variety of foods.
The market leads to an unequal distribution of goods.

runs.text: The government of a prosperous country announced that it would offer free food to its citizens for a year.
What would be the effect of this measure?

cells.text: Agricultural resources would become unlimited.
Human wants would become finite.
More resources would be devoted to food production.
The basic economic problem would be solved.

runs.text: There has been increased concern about the way large firms exploit the environment.
What is the main reason for this concern?

cells.text: Large firms are unprofitable because of diseconomies of scale.
Large firms combine together to fix prices.
The exploitation of resources is expensive.
Unlimited wants will use up the finite resources.

runs.text: What is the best example of the existence of the economic problem?

cells.text: A government provides accommodation for all those who are homeless.
A police force has a lengthening list of unsolved crimes.
Janitha hands her homework in at the last permitted deadline.
Musa completes his journey without putting petrol in his car.

runs.text: Which combination of terms gives the general definition of the economic problem?

cells.text: bigger families, less food, starvation
falling supply, rising demand, shortage
higher population, fewer jobs, unemployment
limited resources, unlimited wants, scarcity

runs.text: What best describes the problem of scarcity?

cells.text: All consumer wants must be satisfied.
All resources are free at the point of use.
There are limited resources and unlimited wants.
There are unlimited resources and limited wants.

runs.text: What is the cause of the economic problem facing all countries?

cells.text: climate change and global warming
significant quantities of unemployed resources
uneven distribution of income and wealth
unlimited wants in relation to limited resources

runs.text: In economics, natural sunlight is classified as a free good.
What is the reason for this?

cells.text: Sunlight is a gift of nature.
Sunlight is a renewable resource.
There is no opportunity cost of using sunlight.
Unlimited amounts of sunlight can be consumed.

runs.text: Economics textbooks identify the existence of scarcity as the basic economic problem.
What is it that makes scarcity a problem?

cells.text: It can cause inflation and unemployment.
It is impossible to satisfy unlimited wants.
It is the first priority of governments.
It only affects the richest countries.

runs.text: What is the basic problem facing all economies?

cells.text: how to achieve a stable balance of payments
how to maximise tax revenues
how to reach full employment
how to use scarce resources

runs.text: What do economies aim to achieve in tackling the economic problem of scarcity?

cells.text: equal balance between public and private sectors
equal reward for equal effort
increased competition in the use of resources
optimum allocation of finite resources

runs.text: Hospital services are provided by the government and paid for through taxation. People cannot always get the treatment they require because of long waiting lists.
Of what is this an example?

cells.text: external cost
market system
perfectly inelastic supply
scarcity

runs.text: What identifies a finite resource?

cells.text: The resource does not renew itself.
The supply of the resource is greater than demand.
There is no opportunity cost for the resource.
There is unlimited supply of the resource.

runs.text: A natural resource was discovered in a country. The exploitation of this resource allowed the country to double its gross domestic product within ten years.
Why did this not solve the basic economic problem?

cells.text: Exploiting the resource required high expenditure on capital equipment.
Exploiting the resource caused significant environmental damage.
Gross domestic product was unevenly distributed in the country.
Wants still exceeded the resources available to meet those wants.

runs.text: What is the basic economic problem?

cells.text: excess supply of goods and services
lack of profits
recession
scarcity of resources

runs.text: What causes economic agents to make choices?

cells.text: limited needs and wants
the existence of finite resources
the existence of free goods
the market mechanism

runs.text: Why do consumers have to make choices when spending their income?

cells.text: Advertising encourages consumer spending.
Consumers have unlimited incomes.
Consumer wants cannot all be satisfied with their income.
Not all products will be attractive to consumers.
